Fix contactor status display showing incorrect state when contactors open

The web interface was incorrectly displaying "PRECHARGE" when contactors_engaged == 0,
which actually represents DISCONNECTED state with all contactors open. This caused
confusion when the inverter requested contactors to open - the GPIO pins would be OFF
but the web interface would show "PRECHARGE".

Changes:
- Updated webserver.cpp to correctly map contactors_engaged values:
  * 0 = OFF (DISCONNECTED) - previously showed "PRECHARGE"
  * 1 = ON (COMPLETED)
  * 2 = OFF (FAULT)
  * 3 = PRECHARGE (new state for precharge sequence)

- Updated comm_contactorcontrol.cpp to set contactors_engaged = 3 during the
  precharge sequence (START_PRECHARGE, PRECHARGE, POSITIVE states) so the web
  interface accurately reflects when contactors are energizing.

This ensures the web interface always displays the actual GPIO contactor states
throughout the entire contactor control sequence.

Fix SD Init bug when SD missing or is corrupted

There are cases when SD logging is enabled without a phisical SD card
present or the SD card is corrupted. In these cases a crash could happen
because the SD init routine is not checking the result of init_sdcard()
function and this could lead into different crashes depending on the case.

This fix is checking if the SD card was correctly initialized , otherwise
it will delete the logging buffers, disable the SD logging and delete the
logging task to save some memory

Optimize for size and debug

As there is intense need for flash space on smaller flash devices
optimizations are needed on the code and also on the way the compiler
works.
This commit is dealing with the copiler flag optimization for space and
also improoving the code for clean and predictive debug.
The most important flag that actually reduced the flash size of the binary
is "-fno-exceptions". C++ exceptions (throw/try/catch) are not used in Battery
Emulator or libraries.
The C++ exception support
 - increases binary size significantly
 - requires extra runtime support
 - complicates stack unwinding on a small MCU
Let's get rid of it and save ~10% of flash space ;)

BMW-PHEV: Add CAN-based contactor close support (0x10B + 0x53A)

Implements contactor close control for the BMW PHEV battery, modelled on
the iX implementation.

Changes:
- Override supports_contactor_close() → true; add request_open/close_contactors()
  WebUI API so the generic advanced UI buttons appear automatically.
- Add contactorCloseReq state driven by edge-detected inverter request
  (inverter_allows_contactor_closing) and user WebUI request.
- 0x10B (20ms) now gates close on: contactor_control_enabled == false AND
  contactorCloseReq == true AND startup_counter >= 160 (~3.2s boot delay).
  Previously auto-closed unconditionally after the startup timer regardless
  of any request or GPIO config.
- Add 0x53A (200ms) streaming STATE D (steady/on) as the associated vehicle
  contactor state indication. Bench testing confirmed 0x10B is the actual
  contactor driver; 0x53A is a state reflection (contactors close even while
  0x53A streams STATE A).
- Document all four observed 0x53A states (A/B/C/D) and the full 0x10B
  close conditions in the INFO block for future reference.

Big thanks to Fare for both the vehicle logs & finding the importance of the 53A message!

BMW-PHEV: Add/update DTC descriptions in HTML

- Update 0x21F1F6 description wording to match BMW ISTA ("switching
  contactors" not "switch contactors")
- Add 0x21F00F (cooling system: refrigerant shutoff valve, line
  disconnection) to the Cooling System block
- Add 14 new CAN missing-message fault codes (CAD4xx / CAC47C) as a
  dedicated "Missing CAN Messages (SME receiver)" block:
    CAD415 - ETS HV battery specs (0x10B), transmitter EME
    CAD408 - vehicle condition (0x3A0), transmitter BDC
    CAD426 - state of charge (0x3E), transmitter EME
    CAD416 - status of electric motor 1 (0x10B) signal invalid, EME
    CAD402 - relative time (0x328), transmitter KOMBI
    CAD429 - driving information forecast (0x3CA), transmitter KOMBI
    CAD413 - HV battery specification (0x433), transmitter EME
    CAD401 - ambient temperature (0x2CA), transmitter KOMBI
    CAD40A - vehicle speed (0x1A1), transmitter DSC
    CAD409 - HV battery cooling enable (0x37B), transmitter IHKA
    CAD40B - km-reading/range (0x330), transmitter KOMBI
    CAD405 - OBD diagnosis engine control (0x3E8), transmitter EME
    CAC47C - SME K-CAN9 communication fault
    CAD404 - request HV battery (0xCC), transmitter EME
    CAD403 - VCU_FD01 (0xB5), transmitter EDME

- Add supports_read_DTC() / read_DTC() overrides so the generic advanced

BMW-PHEV: Fix BMS reset UDS frame length byte

BMW_6F1_REQUEST_HARD_RESET had an incorrect ISO-TP length byte of 0x03
(claiming 3 payload bytes) but only carried 2 UDS bytes (0x11 0x01),
causing the SME to reject the request.

Fix: change length byte 0x03 → 0x02, matching the standard UDS ECU
hard reset framing used by all other requests on this bus and consistent
with the iX implementation (BMWiX_6F4_REQUEST_HARD_RESET).

BMW-PHEV: Add vehicle environment frames + fix on-demand DTC read

The SME raises CAD4xx "No message" DTCs when expected vehicle bus frames
are absent. Add the captured frames and transmit the safe (static) ones.

Transmitted:
- 0x3A0 (CAD408, vehicle condition / BDC) - 1000ms, static
- 0x3CA (CAD429, driving-info forecast / KOMBI) - 1000ms, static
- 0x3E8 (CAD405, OBD diagnosis engine ctrl / EME) - 1000ms, static
- 0x2CA (CAD401, ambient temperature / KOMBI) - 1000ms, static 0x6E
  = 15C (in-range, avoids cold/hot charge derating). byte = (T+40)*2.

Defined for reference but NOT transmitted (need a rolling counter on the
real bus; sending frozen risks a "signal invalid" DTC):
- 0x1A1 (CAD40A, vehicle speed / DSC) - byte1 lo-nibble rolls 0..E
- 0x328 (CAD402, relative time / KOMBI) - byte0 seconds counter
- 0x433 (CAD413, HV-battery spec / EME) - byte1 toggles 0x0C<->0x0D

Reference only (not transmitted):
- 0x37B (CAD409, enable HV-battery cooling / IHKA)
- 0x10B (CAD415/416) already sent as the contactor driver (20ms loop)

Added a VEHICLE TX MAP table to the INFO block documenting each frame's
DTC, transmitter, DLC, sample payload, period, send status, and the
counter/CRC logic required to enable the ones not yet transmitted. Noted
that the source canlog was captured during a charging session, so the
vehicle-condition payloads reflect that state.

Fix on-demand DTC read:
Moving DTC read from the periodic slow-UDS poll to a single on-demand
button exposed a race - the read shares one global UDS context with the
200ms/1000ms polls, so a colliding poll corrupted the DTC multiframe
reassembly with no retry. Now pause the fast/slow UDS polls while a user
DTC read is in flight (dtcReadInProgress), clear it when the DTC response
is parsed, with a 2.5s timeout safety net so polling always resumes.

BMW-PHEV: Revert on-demand DTC read, restore UDS poll loop

Revert the on-demand "Read DTC" button approach - it shared the single
global UDS context with the periodic 200ms/1000ms polls, so a colliding

BMW PHEV: Fix UDS poll collisions, DTC read, 0x53A idle state, balancing MQTT

UDS poll collision fixes
- Guard both fast (200ms) and slow (1000ms) UDS polls behind
  gUDSContext.UDS_inProgress so a new First Frame cannot clobber a
  multi-frame response that is still being reassembled. This was
  preventing long DTC reads (10+ faults) from ever completing.
- Add 500ms UDS_REASSEMBLY_TIMEOUT_MS to abandon stalled reassembly
  so a lost frame cannot wedge polling permanently.
- Add 1s UDS_ONE_SHOT_SILENCE_MS window after Clear DTC / BMS Reset
  so the response has time to arrive before the next poll fires.

DTC single-frame response handling
- Add SF handler branch for 0x59 0x02 responses so short/empty DTC
  replies (e.g. "59 02 FF" = no faults) are now parsed and update
  dtc_count/dtc_last_read_millis. Previously they were silently dropped.

DTC HTML - last read time when no faults
- Show "Last Read: Xs ago" on the DTC section even when dtc_count == 0,
  guarded by dtc_last_read_millis > 0 to avoid a spurious timestamp
  before the first successful read.

0x53A contactor state message
- Changed from always streaming STATE D (steady/on) to tracking
  contactorCloseReq: STATE A (00 01) when contactors not requested,
  STATE D (84 00) when requested, keeping it in sync with 0x10B.

Balancing status → MQTT
- Map PHEV raw balancing_status values to datalayer.battery.status
  .balancing_status enum so MQTT receives the correct string. Previously
  only datalayer_extended.bmwphev.balancing_status was written (HTML
  only); the shared datalayer field was never updated.

New BALANCING_STATUS_BLOCKED enum
- Added BALANCING_STATUS_BLOCKED = 4 to balancing_status_enum.
- PHEV raw value 2 ("cells not at rest") now maps to BLOCKED instead
  of UNKNOWN. MQTT publishes "Blocked".
- No impact on existing integrations (iX, i3) - new value appended,
  no existing integer assignments changed.

BMW PHEV: contactor-close handshake, 0x328 clock, balancing routine control + UI

Idle-state and contactor-close fixes for the BMW PHEV battery, plus balancing controls.

Contactor close (0x53A) handshake
- Add a 0x53A state machine (IDLE -> CLOSE_REQ -> ESCALATED -> STEADY) that replays the OEM
  open->close sequence: STATE B (close requested) is announced for ~3.5s before 0x10B drives
  the contactors closed.
- Gate 0x10B contactor close on the state machine reaching ESCALATED/STEADY so we no longer
  jump straight to closed, fixing the intermittent open->close safety warning.

0x328 relative-time clock (ported from i3)
- Transmit 0x328 every 1000ms with a live, incrementing counter: bytes 0-3 = seconds since
  system start (LE), bytes 4-5 = absolute day counter (LE, rolls at 86400s).
- A frozen/absent clock was a likely trigger for the idle precharge block after ~10 min.

Balancing routine control (UDS 0xAD6B)
- The balancing start request is a UDS startRoutine that latches in the SME until explicitly
  stopped. Previously it was sent unconditionally every 10s, so once cells reached rest
  (~10 min idle) the latched routine executed, starting balancing and blocking precharge.
- Gate startRoutine behind user_requests_balancing; send stopRoutine otherwise to keep the
  SME in sync with our intent.
- Send stopRoutine once at boot to clear any routine left latched from a prior run.

Balancing UI
- Add supports_balancing_request() capability that renders independent, always-visible
  Start and Stop Balancing buttons (vs the single toggle), wired to user_requests_balancing.
- PHEV now uses these dual buttons on the advanced page; i3 toggle behaviour unchanged.

BMW PHEV: add isolation test, balancing UDS guards, and status UI

Add an isolation-test request and harden the balancing/UDS request flow on
the BMW PHEV battery.

- Balancing requests (start/stop) now set the UDS one-shot silence timer
  (uds_one_shot_sent_ms) like the DTC/BMS reset commands, so the SME routine
  reply is not clobbered by the periodic UDS polls.
- Add isolation test capability: BMWPHEV_6F1_REQUEST_ISOLATION_TEST (0xAD61)
  startRoutine, sent as a guarded one-shot when requested. Wired through a new
  UserRequestIsolationTest flag in DATALAYER_INFO_BMWPHEV, supports_isolation_test()/
  request_isolation_test() base virtuals + PHEV override, and an "Isolation Test"

BMW PHEV: send guarded balancing stops before contactor close

Ensure balancing is reliably cancelled before a contactor close, since balancing
blocks contactor close in the SME and single sends can be missed.

- 10s UDS loop continues sending startRoutine/stopRoutine every cycle, selected
  by user_requests_balancing, so the SME state is kept in sync either way.
- On a contactor close request (PhevCloseContactors): clear user_requests_balancing
  and arm a pre-close phase that sends several guarded stopRoutine frames
  (PHEV_PRE_CLOSE_STOP_COUNT, one per UDS-guard window). Each send sets the UDS
  one-shot silence timer so it isn't clobbered by polls.
- Hold off 0x10B close (allow_can_close) until all pre-close stop frames have been
  sent (phev_pre_close_stops_remaining == 0), overlapping the existing ~3.5s 0x53A
  announce window.

BMW PHEV: Linting fix2

BMW PHEV: send balancing start/stop as a guarded burst on request change

Replace the periodic 10s balancing send with an edge-triggered guarded burst,
mirroring the pre-close stop burst. A single periodic send was getting missed
by the SME.

- On a change to user_requests_balancing, fire PHEV_BALANCING_BURST_COUNT guarded
  frames of the new desired state (startRoutine when requested, stopRoutine when
  cancelled), one per UDS-guard window (PHEV_BALANCING_BURST_INTERVAL_MS). Each
  send sets the UDS one-shot silence timer so it isn't clobbered by polls.
- Remove the balancing start/stop send from the 10s loop (loop kept, now empty).
- Add burst state members (phev_last_balancing_request, phev_balancing_burst_start,
  phev_balancing_bursts_remaining, phev_balancing_burst_last_ms) and constants.

BMW PHEV: fix current reading displayed at 10x

Fix unit conversion for current_dA assignment. battery_current is in milliAmps
(mA, after the *10 scaling in the CAN parse), but current_dA expects deciAmps
(dA). Divide by 100 to convert correctly: mA / 100 = dA.

This fixes current readings being displayed 10x higher than actual.

BMW PHEV: fix pre-contactor voltage parse (DLC mismatch)

The pre-contactor voltage UDS response (0xDDB4) has DLC 7, not 8. The parse
condition was checking DLC == 8, so the frame never matched and battery_voltage
remained at its default 370.0V instead of reading the actual pack voltage.

Change the condition to DLC == 7 to match the actual response format.

BMW PHEV: ignore redundant contactor close requests when already closed

Pressing close contactor while contactors are already closed (phev_53a_state
== STEADY) was restarting the close handshake, re-arming the pre-close stop
burst, and causing a ~3.5s open/reclose cycle.

Add an early bail-out check: if contactorCloseReq is already set and the state
machine is STEADY (fully closed), ignore the request. This prevents unnecessary
state resets and stop bursts.

BMW PHEV: use broadcast 0x112 for pack voltage, eliminate UDS polling

Replace the slow UDS polled voltage (0xDDB4) with live 20ms broadcast from 0x112
D3:D4. The broadcast already carries the pack voltage at 0.1 V/bit LE and matches
the UDS value exactly (368.2-368.3 V).

- Read battery_voltage directly from 0x112 (D3:D4, LE), no division needed
  (raw value is already in dV, not centivolt)
- Comment out the old UDS parse for 0xDDB4 (DEPRECATED)
- Remove BMWPHEV_6F1_REQUEST_MAINVOLTAGE_PRECONTACTOR from the fast-poll array
  (reduce UDS traffic from 5 fast requests to 4)
- Reduce UDS_REQUESTS_FAST array size from 5 to 4
- Add comment to 0x430 clarifying that prediction voltages are load estimates,
  not hard limits (hard limits come from UDS 0xDD7E)

Result: voltage now updates every 20ms (broadcast) instead of ~1s (UDS poll cycle)

BMW PHEV: reduce contactor close 0x53A announce from 3.5s to 1s

The 0x53A STATE B close-requested announce was held for 3.5s before escalating
to STATE C/D and allowing 0x10B to drive the contactors. This was overly
conservative; the OEM handshake works reliably with 1s.

Reduce CONTACTOR_CLOSE_REQUEST_DURATION_MS from 3500ms to 1000ms. Total close
time now dominated by the pre-close balancing stop burst (~3s at 1s intervals
between 3 frames), making the whole sequence faster and more responsive.

fix(kostal-rs485): don't call battery->update_values() on cyclic poll

KostalInverterProtocol::receive() called battery->update_values() on every
cyclic-data request (code 0x44a), in addition to the core loop's regular 1 Hz
call. That runs the battery's update_values() roughly twice per second, so any
per-second/time-based logic inside it (timers, staleness/keep-alive counters)
advances at ~2x the intended rate. No other inverter integration calls into the
battery object like this — the existing TODO already flagged it as a bad idea.

Remove the call. The core loop owns the battery update cadence; the inverter
reads the datalayer that the core loop already refreshes.

test: ensure compatibility with AppleClang/macOS

The unit-test mocks enumerated fixed-width int64_t/uint64_t overloads for
String (test/emul/WString.h) and Logging::print/println. On LP64 Linux uint64_t
is `unsigned long`. On macOS uint64_t is `unsigned long long`, leaving the native
`unsigned long` uncovered, so the call was an ambiguous overload (rejected by
AppleClang 21). Spell the four distinct native 64-bit-capable types
(long / unsigned long / long long / unsigned long long) instead, covering
int64_t/uint64_t on every platform with no duplicate definition.

sma: startup grace period for SMA inverter CAN watchdog

SMA inverters can take a while to boot before they start sending CAN, so
the inverter watchdog (CAN_inverter_still_alive, 60s) would raise the
EVENT_CAN_INVERTER_MISSING error at startup before the inverter is even up.

Add a needs_can_startup_grace() predicate to InverterProtocol (default
false) and override it to true in SmaInverterBase, covering all SMA
variants.

Guard display against SMALL_FLASH_DEVICE

### What
This PR encloses all functionality related to the I2C SSD1306 display between #ifndef SMALL_FLASH_DEVICE / #endif guards, including its web UI settings options

### Why
To be able to free up flash space on memory-constrained targets (LilyGo T-CAN485, devkit builds with SMALL_FLASH_DEVICE).

### How
Follows the existing SMALL_FLASH_DEVICE pattern already used in comm_rs485.cpp, wifi.cpp, and battery files. No #else branches or stubs needed — call sites are guarded directly.
Two things are intentionally not guarded:

- The I2C_DISPLAY_SSD1306 enumerator values in types.h: the T-CAN485 SD-card pin functions in hw_lilygo.h compare against them to resolve the GPIO 14/15 pin-sharing conflict, and bare enum values cost no flash.
- Those pin-conflict checks themselves: if a device's NVS still holds GPIOOPT4 = 1 from a previously flashed full build, the SD card correctly stays disabled instead of driving pins wired to a display. The display simply won't run.

Fix Pylon protocol compatibility with GCE and similar BMS

Three related fixes for BMS that use the Pylontech HV CAN protocol but
deviate slightly from the reference encoding (observed on GCE HV BMS):

- Discharge current limit (frame 0x4211 bytes 6-7): some BMS encode this
  with a positive offset (30000 + I) like the charge limit, instead of
  the standard negative offset. The old `-(value - 30000)` then produced
  a large negative number that underflowed the unsigned datalayer field,
  reporting ~4294959 kW max discharge power to the inverter. Using abs()
  yields the correct magnitude for both encodings.

- Design voltage: the BMS-announced charge/discharge cutoffs (frame
  0x4220) overwrote the user-configured pack voltage limits on every
  update cycle, so explicit min/max settings had no effect. The cutoffs
  now only apply when the user has left the corresponding limit at 0.

- Battery info page: expose the highest/lowest cell number and hottest/
  coldest temperature sensor index (already present in frames 0x4231/
  0x4241 but previously discarded), and show the BMS cutoffs in volts
  plus the design voltage range actually in use.

Make core-task CAN logging non-blocking to prevent task overruns

- SD CAN logging: build the whole line, single zero-timeout ringbuffer
  send per frame (was up to 9 sends with 2ms timeout each, ~18ms worst
  case blocking in the core task). Dropped frames are counted and
  reported as a gap marker in the log.
- add_log_to_buffer: zero timeout, and remove logging.println from the
  failure path (recursed via Logging::write back into itself while the
  buffer was full -> stack overflow when the SD writer stalled).
- USB CAN logging: single snprintf-built line written only when the TX
  buffer has room (was ~15 blocking Serial.print calls per frame).
  Serial TX buffered at 1024 bytes so bursts absorb and CAN-FD lines
  fit; dropped frames reported as a gap marker.

Skip unchanged values in NVS settings store to reduce flash writes

saveUInt/saveBool/saveString read the old value but wrote to NVS
unconditionally, so every store_settings() call rewrote every key.
Each put is a synchronous flash operation that suspends the cache on
both cores, and the churn accelerates NVS page GC (a full page erase,
the longest stall of all). Now all save* methods only write when the
value actually changed, matching what saveInt already did.

Also fixes a latent bug in saveInt: change detection used a sentinel
default (INT32_MAX), so saving a value equal to the sentinel into a
missing key was silently skipped and never persisted. All methods now
use an explicit isKey() check instead, which also covers stored false
booleans and empty strings being mistaken for missing keys.

Apply user current caps to low pass filter input

Cap the filter input with max_user_set_charge/discharge_dA (converted
via pack voltage, design-voltage fallback) before blending, so the ramp
time constant acts on the effective range instead of being accelerated
by headroom above the cap. Also makes runtime cap increases ramp
smoothly. BYD-Modbus driver-side min() becomes idempotent.

Make USB debug logging non-blocking to prevent task overruns

Logging::write, Logging::printf and add_timestamp all wrote to Serial
unconditionally. With USB logging active and a host that stops draining
the port, the TX buffer fills and every DEBUG_PRINTF from the core task
(battery/inverter update paths) blocks, delaying the 10ms tasks and
raising EVENT_TASK_OVERRUN.

All three sites now route through a shared usb_log_write() helper that
only writes when availableForWrite() reports room, mirroring the pattern
already merged for CAN frame logging in comm_can.cpp. Dropped output is
reported with a marker line once the port drains, and the marker is
always flushed before output resumes so the gap appears at the right
place in the log.

Behavior change: a stalled host now means drop-with-marker instead of
block-until-delivered. With this, no logging sink (SD, USB CAN frames,
USB debug, web, syslog) can block the core task.

Fix missing newline on truncated log lines

Logging::printf caps a line at MAX_LINE_LENGTH_PRINTF (128) characters.
When a message is longer, vsnprintf drops the remainder including the
trailing newline, so previous_message_was_newline stays false and the
next message is appended to that line without its own timestamp. The
next message can be logged hours later, which makes the log misleading
about when it happened.

Use the vsnprintf return value to detect truncation and terminate the
line explicitly. Also guard against a non-positive result, which
previously indexed message_buffer[-1]; the write() path already has the
equivalent size check.

Reproduced with EVENT_WIFI_AP_PROVISION_TIMEOUT, whose message is 170
characters.

Make absolute millis() comparisons wrap-safe (49.7-day rollover)

millis() wraps at 2^32 ms, about 49.7 days. Five sites compared it as
an absolute since-boot value instead of using wrap-safe arithmetic:

- BMW-I3-BATTERY.cpp / CMP-SMART-CAR-BATTERY.cpp wakeup gating: benign
  in practice (the GPIO output latch holds through the 1 s post-wrap
  window; worst case is a delayed HIGH-restore) - hygiene fix.
- KIA-E-GMP-BATTERY.cpp voltage-limit one-shot: benign (latch set long
  before wrap) - hygiene fix.
- safety.cpp inverter startup grace: real - for inverters using the
  startup grace window (SMA family), a NEW inverter-comms loss
  beginning right after the wrap is detected up to 5 minutes late
  because the grace window re-arms.
- Software.cpp remote-limit expiry: real in both directions - the
  timestamp + timeout sum overflows near the wrap so freshly set
  remote limits expire immediately, and after currentMillis wraps,
  stale limits can persist up to another 49.7 days.

Since-boot gates now use the in-tree monotonic millis64() (already used
by the event system); the remote-limit expiry uses wrap-safe unsigned
subtraction, which needs no 64-bit math.

Found while investigating #2390. Deliberately not claimed as a fix for
that report: the emulator holds the pack awake far beyond an ECU's
designed ignition-cycle uptime, and a 32-bit ms counter wrapping inside
the SME itself matches the 50-day fingerprint and the power-cycle
recovery - which no emulator-side change can prevent.

Note on tests: the host test suite cannot exercise the 32-bit wrap -
unsigned long is 64-bit on the host, so the emulated millis() never
truncates. Suite stays green as a no-regression check.

FoxESS battery: refresh CAN keep-alive and stop overwriting BMS-reported voltage limits

Two defects affecting every FoxESS battery user, found investigating
the EP11 report in #1664:

1. The driver never refreshed CAN_battery_still_alive - the only
   battery driver without a single refresh site. EVENT_CAN_BATTERY_MISSING
   (ERROR level) therefore fired 60 seconds after boot regardless of
   live traffic, forcing system_status to FAULT, charge/discharge
   limits to zero, and the inverter to see a dead battery. The counter
   is now refreshed in the eight periodic 0x187x status cases -
   recognized traffic only, per the still-alive test contract that
   bogus frames must not renew the counter.

2. update_values() re-applied the hardcoded HS-series pack table every
   cycle, overwriting the design voltage limits the BMS itself reports
   in 0x1872 (BMS_Limits) - the frame handler wrote them, then the next
   update cycle clobbered them. Packs outside the HS table (EP-series,
   e.g. EP11 at ~398 V vs the HS15.6 table's 350.4 V max) tripped a
   false BATTERY_OVERVOLTAGE that zeroed charge power. The 0x1872
   limits are now authoritative once received; the table remains the
   fallback before the first 0x1872 and stays the only source for
   number_of_cells.

unfixed driver, and the limits test pins 0x1872 survival through
update_values() plus the pre-0x1872 table fallback.

Equipment stop: wait for zero current before opening contactors (bounded)

Equipment stop zeroes the power limits and dropped all contactor
outputs in the same 10 ms tick - faster than any inverter can ramp
down, so the contactors opened under load (arcing/welding risk, the
scenario described in #1750).

The graceful machinery already exists everywhere else: the pause state
machine only reports PAUSED below 1.8 A, the BMS reset waits for zero
current with a 10 s give-up 'so we don't weld the contactors', and
graceful restart waits for PAUSED. This applies the same pattern to
the e-stop path: since every e-stop entry point (button, MQTT, web)
also issues a battery pause, the COMPLETED state now holds until the
pause reaches PAUSED or a 10 s timeout, then opens. On the timeout
path EVENT_ERROR_OPEN_CONTACTOR is raised with data=1 so a forced
open under load is visible in the event log.

Inverter-commanded opening keeps today's immediate behavior (the
inverter has already stopped power before revoking permission), and
the latched FAULT shutdown path is untouched.

Adds host tests: hold-under-load with bounded timeout + event,
prompt open when already paused, mid-wait pause completion, and the
immediate inverter-path regression guard.

Add an offgrid setting that downgrades grid-presence faults

An offgrid system has no grid-tied inverter to lose, but losing it is
still reported as an ERROR, which raises system_status to FAULT. That
gates precharge, so a standalone system cannot black start: the battery
will not come up until an inverter it does not have starts talking.

New setting "Inverter is offgrid", default off, so existing installations
behave exactly as before. Any inverter can be run offgrid, so this
describes the installation rather than anything gated on protocol - and
because the core events engine is what consumes it, it is owned core-side
in types.cpp alongside the other core-generic user settings, not by the
inverter registry.

The downgrade is applied where the level is read, from a short allowlist
that starts with EVENT_CAN_INVERTER_MISSING, rather than by editing the
severity table in init_events(). That keeps the declared severity
readable in one place and makes the exception auditable, and it means
what gets aggregated, logged and shown on the events page is the
effective level - not a FAULT that merely displays as a warning.
Extending it later is a matter of adding an event id.

The 300 s SMA grace is left alone; it becomes belt-and-braces rather than
the thing holding this together.

Tests cover both directions plus the allowlist boundary, and the offgrid

Nissan LEAF: classify balancing by change rate, not change recency

The classifier held the pack ACTIVE indefinitely after a balancing session
had clearly finished. The static-poll counter was reset to zero on any
change of the shunt bitmap, so it measured how recently the bitmap moved
rather than how often. A single cell hovering at the balancing threshold
toggles on its own every few polls, which reset the counter before it could
reach the threshold, and the status never returned to BLOCKED.

Count changes over a sliding window of reads instead. BALANCING_CHANGES_FOR
_ACTIVE or more changes within BALANCING_ACTIVITY_WINDOW_POLLS means the LBC
is swapping cell sets regularly and the pack is really balancing; no changes
at all across the whole window means the same set has been held throughout
and the pack is flagged but at rest. Between the two the previous status is
held, so the state does not chatter at the boundary. A change now also has
to move at least BALANCING_SIGNIFICANT_CELL_CHANGES cells to count, which
rejects the single-cell flicker that caused the original problem.

The constants were validated by replaying two days of logged shunt bitmaps
from a 2017 30 kWh pack (719 recorded states, ~73 s poll cadence) through
the classifier. The log contains all three regimes the LBC exhibits:

  housekeeping   0-12 cells flagged (median 0), single-cell flicker
  pending        38-41 cells latched, 2-10 changes/h, 1.0 cells per change
  balancing      32-38 cells, ~90% of polls change, ~3 cells per change

With a window of 12 and 3 significant changes the replay classifies the
7.4 h pending phase and the 7.1 h balancing session cleanly, with no
dropouts and no stuck state.

The replay also showed the READY boundary chattering: outside its balancing
phases the LBC keeps a low-level bleed flickering on 0-2 cells, so a
READY-at-exactly-zero rule flipped READY<->BLOCKED whenever the count
crossed zero - about a hundred transitions over the two days. Fewer than
BALANCING_READY_BELOW_CELLS (4) flagged cells now counts as READY, which the
log separates cleanly (housekeeping tops out around 12 in brief spikes,
real phases never drop below 32) and which cuts the replayed transition
count from 100 to 14 without moving any phase boundary.

Also require all three frames of a group 0x06 response before publishing the
bitmap. A dropped frame previously left part of battery_balancing_shunts[]
holding the previous response, which the classifier saw as a change.

Nissan LEAF: classify balancing by how much the shunt set moves

The classifier counted group 0x06 reads in which at least two shunts
changed, and called the pack ACTIVE once three such reads fell inside a
twelve-read window. Replaying 89 hours of logged shunt bitmaps from a 2017
30 kWh pack shows that this over-reports badly: during a pending phase
about a third of reads move two or more shunts, which is enough to trip the
window, so a nine-hour phase in which the pack was plainly not balancing
was reported as ACTIVE. The replay produced 41 state transitions and broke
both real balancing sessions into fragments.

The logged data separates the two phases cleanly, but by the *magnitude* of
the change rather than its presence:

  pending        0.0 - 1.6 shunts changing per read
  balancing      7.8 - 9.7 shunts changing per read

Count how many shunts change per read and smooth it with an integer
exponential moving average. Above BALANCING_CHURN_ACTIVE (3 shunts per
read) the LBC is bleeding and swapping cells, so the pack is ACTIVE; below
BALANCING_CHURN_IDLE (1.5) it is holding a set at rest, so BLOCKED; between
the two the previous status is held. Replaying the same 89 hours now
reproduces both sessions and both pending phases exactly, with four
transitions, which is the minimum the data admits.

The log also contains a phase in which the LBC flagged every shunt it has
and held that perfectly static for 20.8 hours, entering it in a single poll
and decaying gradually on exit. A rule based on change presence has no way
to tell that from balancing once anything at all flickers; a rule based on
change rate reports it as BLOCKED, which is what it is.

READY is now debounced over BALANCING_READY_DEBOUNCE_READS reads. The log
contains ten single-poll all-clear readings, off-cadence and immediately
followed by a normally populated bitmap, which are incomplete group 0x06
responses rather than a finished balance. Each one previously ended the
phase early and injected two large false change counts, one on the way out
and one on the way back. The read following a low-count one is also
excluded from the rate, since the bitmap it would be compared against is
the suspect sample.

ESPNow: replace the struct protocol with an extensible ESP-NOW v2 TLV format

The v1 implementation broadcast raw datalayer structs byte-for-byte. Any field
added, reordered or resized broke every receiver, and cell voltages had to be
quantized to 20 mV steps to fit the 250 byte ESP-NOW v1 frame.

Replace it with a self-describing key/length/value stream:

* The length lives in the tag byte, encoded independently of the type class, so
  a receiver can skip a record whose *type* it has never seen, not just an
  unknown key. New keys and new types can therefore both be added without
  another compatibility break.
* Cell voltages are sent as raw uint16 millivolts, unquantized, for all three
  batteries, alongside a balancing bitset.
* Everything currently published over MQTT is exposed, plus the emulator-level
  status, link state and event stream.
* ESP-NOW v2 (1470 byte) frames are used when the IDF supports them, detected at
  runtime via esp_now_get_version(). On a v1-only build the cell array is split
  into index-tagged chunks, so the same firmware works either way.
* New ESPNOWMACS setting: a list of receiver MAC addresses shown on the settings
  page only while ESPNow is enabled. Empty keeps the previous broadcast
  behaviour.

Frames are paced one per tick instead of bursting a dozen packets at once, and
serialization uses a single static buffer with no String, printf or allocation
in the send path.

Make core time arithmetic width-deterministic (uint32_t)

millis() is 32 bits wide on the target: the wrap at 2^32 ms IS the
semantics of every timestamp comparison. Declaring time values as
unsigned long makes that width platform-dependent - correct on the
ESP32 where unsigned long is 32-bit, silently different on the 64-bit
host test build, where the wrap never occurs. Consequences: wrap
behavior was untestable (see the discussion on the wrap-safety PR),
and the suite exercised different arithmetic than the target runs.

This narrows the core time-carrying variables to uint32_t:

- Software.cpp: currentMillis, the interval trackers, and the
  update_calculated_values() parameter
- comm_contactorcontrol.cpp: precharge/BMS-reset state machine
  timestamps and the reset-interval helper
- datalayer: remote_set_timestamp / remote_set_timeout
- MyTimer: interval and previous_millis

and moves the remote-limit expiry check into
update_remote_limit_expiry() in safety.cpp so it is reachable from the
host test suite.

With production widths deterministic, the emulated millis() now
truncates to 32 bits exactly like the target, so the host runs the
same arithmetic the ESP32 runs - wrap included. The BMS-reset
overflow tests move from the host's 2^64 boundary to the target's real
2^32 boundary, and new wrap regression tests cover the two real bugs
fixed by the wrap-safety sweep: the SMA startup-grace re-arm and the
remote-limit expiry (both directions of the old overflow).

Driver-level unsigned long usage (including the transmit_can interface
signatures) is deliberately untouched - that sweep is a follow-up.

Depends on the wrap-safety branch (built on top of it).

ESPNow: address review - drop v1 fallback, fix the extended key escape

Two changes from @jonny5532's review:

* Assume ESP-NOW v2. The runtime esp_now_get_version() probe is gone and
  max_payload / cells_per_chunk are now compile-time constants, which is worth
  ~300 bytes of flash on the T485. ESPNOW_MAX_PAYLOAD remains overridable: the
  binding limit in practice is the receiver's buffer, not its silicon, and
  receivers have a real reason to keep that small (ESPHome's espnow component
  defaults to 250 bytes because a 1470 byte buffer costs ~44 KB of heap). The
  index-tagged cell chunking is retained deliberately so lowering that one
  constant is all it takes to talk to such a receiver.

* Move the reserved 16 bit extended key INSIDE the value rather than placing it
  between the key and the tag. As previously documented, a future BE emitting
  key 0xFF would have desynchronised every receiver written against this spec,
  because the byte a receiver reads as the tag would have been half the extended
  key - a bogus length, and every subsequent record lost. With the extended key
  as the first two bytes of the value, the tag stays the second byte of every
  record, so existing receivers skip it correctly by length with no knowledge of
  extended keys at all. No receiver-side change is needed, now or when the
  extended space is eventually used.

ESPNow: report the emulator's IP, SSID and access point state

Adds three keys to the SYSTEM frame so a receiver can show the emulator's
network identity without a second transport:

* 0x10 IP_ADDRESS  - IPv4 as four octets in display order
* 0x11 SSID        - the network the station is joined to
* 0x12 AP_ACTIVE   - whether the emulator's own soft AP is up

IP and SSID are omitted while the station is unassociated, so a receiver can
tell 'not connected' from a stale value.

AP_ACTIVE reads the live Wi-Fi mode rather than wifiap_enabled: the AP is
dropped from the mode when provisioning times out while the setting stays true,
so reporting the setting would misrepresent the device.

The station MAC was already available as key 0x03 and needs no change - it is
also the source address of these frames, which is what a receiver needs to fill
in its own peer list.

Nissan LEAF: classify balancing by how often the shunt set stands still

The classifier measured how many shunts change per group 0x06 read and
smoothed that with a moving average. A 232 hour log from a 2017 30 kWh
pack, covering four complete pending-then-balancing cycles, shows that
this quantity is not stable enough to threshold against.

The problem is that it climbs steadily as a balance proceeds. As cells
converge the flagged set shrinks, and the LBC re-decides a larger share
of a smaller set each read, so the same activity reads as very different
numbers depending on how far along the session is:

  balancing, early    30 flagged, 5.7 shunts changing per read
  balancing, late     18 flagged, 12.5 shunts changing per read

Meanwhile the beginning of each session ramps up gradually, passing
through the thresholds slowly enough that the status flapped. Over the
232 hour log the previous rule produced 126 misclassified reads and
broke the sessions into fragments.

How *often* a read comes back with the shunt set completely unchanged is
far more stable. Across all four balancing sessions it sat at 12% of
reads regardless of pack state or how far the session had progressed,
while every pending phase sat between 82% and 100%. That is a five-fold
separation that does not drift as the session proceeds, so count
unchanged reads over a sliding window of BALANCING_WINDOW_READS instead:
at or above BALANCING_UNCHANGED_FOR_IDLE the LBC is holding a set at
rest, at or below BALANCING_UNCHANGED_FOR_ACTIVE it is bleeding and
re-deciding, and in between the previous status is held.

Replaying the same log now reproduces all four cycles with eight
transitions, which is the minimum the data admits, with no fragmentation
and no flapping at the session starts.

ESPNow: replay the 10 most recent events instead of streaming once

Events were sent once, gated on a watermark, so a receiver that started
after the emulator never saw anything that had already happened. Send the
ESPNOW_EVENT_REPLAY most recent occurrences as an indexed batch instead,
re-sent every ESPNOW_EVENT_CYCLE_MS and immediately when a newer
occurrence appears.

Adds ESPNOW_KEY_EVENT_INDEX (0xA8) and ESPNOW_KEY_EVENT_TOTAL (0xA9);
all but the last frame of a batch set ESPNOW_FLAG_MORE_CHUNKS. Receivers
replace their list per batch rather than appending.

Nissan LEAF: do not report balancing until the window has filled

After a boot or a BMS reset the classifier reported ACTIVE almost
immediately, logging "Balancing has started" and then "Balancing has
ended" a quarter of an hour later once it settled on the real state.

The unchanged-read window starts empty, and an empty window holds zero
unchanged reads. Zero is below BALANCING_UNCHANGED_FOR_ACTIVE, so the
first read that could be compared with a predecessor was enough to
declare the pack actively balancing, whatever it was really doing. A
partly filled window has the same problem: it cannot be told apart from a
window full of changed reads, because both report few unchanged reads.

Track how many reads the window holds and make no classification until it
is full. The status then stays at whatever it was - UNKNOWN after a boot
or a BMS reset - until there is enough history to decide, which takes
BALANCING_WINDOW_READS reads, about a quarter of an hour at the group
0x06 poll rate. The fill counter is cleared alongside the window on a BMS
reset and when a phase ends at READY.

Replaying 232 hours of logged shunt bitmaps is unchanged at 99.86%
against the labelled phases with eight transitions, and now emits four
balancing start and four balancing end events, one pair per real session.
Booting into a static pending phase reports UNKNOWN for sixteen reads and
then BLOCKED, with no events at all, where it previously logged a start
and an end.

handle_contactors() closes the contactors through a timed ladder - negative,

expires, then the resistor is dropped and the coils economized - behind a

the rest of the firmware read, so they are the observable contract.

accident and neither is obviously intended:

- Permission being granted closes the negative contactor on the same pass, so
  START_PRECHARGE is never observable from outside.
- dc_bus_live is computed from the status at the top of the pass, so it lags
  one tick: on the tick that latches a fault shutdown it still reads true,
  even though the contactors have just been driven open.

and still report green - which is exactly how both bugs in the previous commit
reached main.

Nissan LEAF: fix HX decoding on ZE0/AZE0 and expose it over MQTT

The Hx value was read at the ZE1 payload offset (28..29, /102.4) for every
generation. ZE0 and AZE0 answer group 1 with a two-byte-shorter layout where
Hx sits at payload 26..27 and is already scaled in hundredths of a percent, so
those packs read the high half of the next field and always reported 0.

0x2B AZE0, 0x35 ZE1) and store the result as hundredths of a percent, giving
the same resolution LeafSpy shows. Add a Leaf-only 'Hx' MQTT sensor with HA
autodiscovery, omitted until a known layout has been decoded.

MQTT: log publish failures once per outage, fix mislabelled event log

The event publish failure was logged as "Common info MQTT msg could not
be sent". It is emitted from publish_events(), and since publish_values()
bails out on its failure, publish_common_info() is never reached during an

Give every battery its own events, and name the pack that raised them

Follow-up to the temperature fixes on this branch, per review feedback:
the shared EVENT_BATTERY_* events are replaced with per-pack variants
rather than a battery number stored alongside a shared event.

All 19 battery specific events now exist once per pack, as contiguous
EVENT_BATTERY1/2/3_* triplets. set_event(event, data, battery) resolves
the concrete event by adding (battery - 1) to the EVENT_BATTERY1_*
variant; clear_event() and set_event_latched() take the same third
argument, since drivers raise and clear through all three. A driver
instance serves whichever pack it is mounted on, so Battery gains a
battery_index that setup_battery() assigns, and the 45 driver call sites
pass it instead of naming an event statically.

Separate events also let two packs fault at once, which the shared enums
could not represent. check_battery_temperatures() is now a plain per-pack
set/clear loop with no worst-offender selection: battery 1 and battery 2
can both report overheating and both are visible.

Nothing enforces the enum layout the resolver relies on, so static_asserts
in events.cpp fail the build if a triplet stops being contiguous or the

BYD-Modbus: fix inverted charge/discharge sign in two registers

The emulator reported the opposite direction to the inverter in both
registers that carry it, so every charge session looked like a discharge
to a polling Gen24.

Register 303 reports the battery state as bit 7 (normal operation) plus
bit 0 (charging) or bit 1 (discharging), i.e. 128/129/130 for idle/
charging/discharging. The driver built this as 128 + bms_char_dis_status
using the DISCHARGING (1) and CHARGING (2) defines from types.h, whose
values are the inverse of that bit order.

convention, where charging is negative. Captured traffic from a real
Battery-Box Premium HV shows 61760 (-3775W) while the pack charged
against a 4.3kW charge target. datalayer active_power_W uses the
opposite convention and was cast through unchanged. The new helper also
clamps to int16 range - the previous direct cast wrapped and flipped
sign above 32.7kW, which a 34kW pack allowance reaches.

The limit checks compared the actual battery power against limits that
setBatteryPause() zeroes instantly, while the inverter can only see the
new values on its next poll and then still has to ramp down. On a Fronius
GEN24 (5s Modbus poll interval) this window is long enough to exceed the
6-sample debounce, raising EVENT_CHARGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED for an inverter
that is obeying a limit it cannot have read yet.

Both checks also sat inside 'if (active_power_W > 0)' / '< 0', so once the
power settled at exactly 0W - where a pause always ends up - neither the
clear_event() nor the failure-counter reset could ever run. The event
stayed active for the rest of the session and the counter stayed saturated,
so the first sample after resuming charging tripped it again immediately.

pause is requested, the pause state machine is not NORMAL, or the system is
in FAULT, and drop the sign gates so an idle battery always clears the
alert. The unsigned limits are cast before comparison, which the sign gates
were previously providing.

Nissan LEAF: transmit CHG_STA_RQ=01b in 0x1F2

CHG_STA_RQ (Charge_StatusTransitionRequest) sits in bits 6-5 of byte 2
of 0x1F2 and was left at 00b ("No request"). The Nissan battery control
specification has the VCM raise it to 01b ("Normal charge") as part of
the start-up sequence and hold it there for the whole of normal
operation, which is what the LBC expects to see from a running vehicle.

The low nibble of byte 7 is the Nissan nibble checksum over the rest of
the message, so the twenty precomputed values in the 0x1F2 pattern each
move by the two nibbles that byte 2 gained. No runtime cost: the frame
is still a table lookup, nothing is calculated per message.

The Leaf PDM charger path builds its own 0x1F2 and already sets byte 2
to 0x20 with a recalculated checksum, so it is unaffected.

Nissan LEAF: re-read the poll-once groups after a BMS reset

Groups 0x62 (AC and quick charge counts), 0x84 (serial number) and 0x83
(part number) are asked for only until they answer, and then dropped
from the rotation so the recurring groups come round faster. That state
was only ever established at boot, so after a BMS reset the values on
the battery info page stayed the ones read before the power cycle and
the new LBC session was never queried for them.

The reset branch in transmit_can() now arms a one pass re-poll and
re-arms the startup burst, so the three groups are asked again a couple
of seconds after the LBC returns. Nothing is skipped during that pass,
so the burst counter reaching zero means every group has been asked
exactly once, which is what ends it. Previous values remain on display
until each fresh reply overwrites them, and the boot path behaves
exactly as before.

Costs one bool of RAM.

Stop starting an automatic precharge that is aborted on the next tick

The AUTO_PRECHARGE_IDLE start gate required only start_precharging and the
inverter permission, while AUTO_PRECHARGE_PRECHARGING aborts back to idle
when the system is not ACTIVE, an equipment stop is active, or the BMS is
not standby/active. Whenever one of the conditions the start gate did not
check was the blocking one, the sequence started, was aborted on the next
tick, and started again - and since entering the sequence drives the
precharge PWM and switches the inverter-disconnect contactor, on the 10 ms
core loop that is a continuous switching cycle rather than a one-off. It
was reported as an audible contactor rattle on a MEB + SMA setup during
black start, and the same asymmetry applies during an equipment stop.

Both sides now share one predicate, so a sequence only starts under the
conditions it needs to keep running. Sequences that used to start and
abort within a tick no longer start; nothing that completes today is
affected, since these are the conditions it already had to satisfy to
survive its first tick. The timeout / BMS-fault path to
AUTO_PRECHARGE_FAILURE and the restart-after-BMS-reset path in
AUTO_PRECHARGE_COMPLETED are unchanged.

digitalWrite now records pin writes, so the tests can assert that the
contactor is never switched while the sequence cannot run, not merely that
the state variable stays put.

OTA: confirm a new image only after the system has actually run

A firmware update that cannot run is permanent today: the board boot-loops
and the only way out is USB, which is why the advice for "bricked by
update" has become "erase the flash and reconfigure", losing every setting.

That is not for want of a rollback mechanism. CONFIG_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE is
already on and the bootloader already runs a new image as PENDING_VERIFY,
restoring the previous one if that boot resets before the app confirms
itself. What closes the window is arduino-esp32: initArduino() calls
esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback() before setup() runs, so an update
is confirmed before a single line of this firmware has executed - and every
crash worth rolling back for happens after that point.

This takes the framework's own opt-out, the weak verifyRollbackLater()
hook, and moves confirmation to where it can mean something: the image is
confirmed once the running system has held together for 42 seconds.

Reaching the end of setup() only says the drivers were constructed. The
failures that justify a rollback happen after that - the first frames
parsed, the first MQTT or HTTP exchange, a watchdog trip under real load.
42 s also clears STA association, TLS-MQTT and autodiscovery bring-up.

The check is one guarded compare at an unconditional point in the 1 ms core
task: both sub-tasks alternating for 42 s is the strongest liveness witness
the firmware has, since it means CAN is being serviced and the task
watchdog fed every pass. It only sets a flag. The write happens in ordinary
main-task context from loop(), because confirming is itself a flash write
and belongs on the same path as every other runtime flash write rather than
being initiated from the core tick.

Criteria deliberately rejected: "all RTOS tasks started" - starting is
cheap, surviving under load is the signal; anything externally dependent
(CAN frames seen, WiFi up) - a bench board with no bus, or an offline
install, must still be able to confirm, or every reboot reverts a good
image forever.

A deliberate restart inside the window keeps the update: the web-UI restart
path confirms first if the system is healthy, then reboots. Panics,
watchdog resets and brownouts still revert.

The behaviour change, stated plainly: an image that dies at t = 30 s, or a
power cut inside the window, now rolls back where previously it would have
been kept. That is the intent, but it is a real change and not only an
improvement.

Cost is +1,072 B of flash on esp32devkit_330, baseline and subject built
back-to-back from wiped build directories in one lock hold. No sdkconfig
change - the flag was never off.

Add BYD automatic top-of-charge with native BMS termination

Lets the BYD Atto 3 BMS terminate the charge itself and recalibrate SOC,
instead of BE stopping the charge at its own cell clamp. BE runs a real
charge session on the pack bus, in place on an already closed pack
(0x86 -> 0x85 -> 0x84, no contactor movement), using only
0x24A/0x47E/0x36A/0x36D.

The session auto-arms on sustained charge current and re-arms only after
a real discharge; a refused grant backs off for 15 minutes. It owns the
taper from cell max 3500mV up to the observed 3742-3753mV termination
band, while below 3500mV the BMS advisory still governs power. The
outcome is reported through EVENT_BYD_CHARGE_TERMINATED, the More Battery
Info page, and eight new charge_* MQTT sensors.

On by default. Needs the pack case isolated from earth, since an
insulation fault keeps the BMS out of the charge context.

fix(modbus): FC06 response must echo the register address

A Modbus FC06 (Write Single Register) response is a byte-for-byte echo of
the request:

    [slaveID][0x06][addrHi][addrLo][valHi][valLo]

ModbusInverterProtocol::FC06() built only:

    [slaveID][0x06][valHi][valLo]

omitting the address, so the response was 4 bytes instead of 6. FC03 in the
same file builds its response correctly, which is what makes the omission
easy to miss.

Masters that validate the echo reject the short form. Observed with a Delta
E6-TL-US: its boot handshake writes six configuration registers over FC06
and will not proceed unless each is echoed in full, leaving the battery
unconfigured.

Ground truth from a real device: an LG RESU10H Prime answering that inverter
echoes the complete request on every write. 21 writes captured 2026-08-26
across four inverter power cycles, e.g.

    request  0f 06 044e 1004 <crc>      (reg 1102 <- 4100)
    response 0f 06 044e 1004 <crc>      identical

This affects every inverter protocol built on ModbusInverterProtocol, not
only the Delta.

Locks the FC06 fix with four tests:

  * every write of a real captured boot handshake round-trips byte-for-byte
  * the written value is stored, including a register written twice
  * an out-of-range address still returns ILLEGAL_DATA_ADDRESS

start, so this pins behaviour to a real implementation rather than to a
reading of the spec.

Nissan LEAF: read SOH, Hx, capacity and 12V from the LBC health block

Adds group 0x61 to the polling rotation and takes state of health from it
at hundredths of a percent, instead of the whole-percent value broadcast in
0x5BC. Hx moves to the same block on ZE0/AZE0; ZE1 keeps the group 0x01
decode it has today. Pack capacity in Ah and the 12 V level are decoded and
shown on the More Battery Info page.

The health block is the only group reply longer than 255 bytes, so its first
frame announces itself as 1L LL rather than 10 LL. The group latch is masked
and the announced length widened to the full 12-bit field so it is picked up
at all, and a per-reply frame counter replaces the ISO-TP sequence number for
identifying payload offsets, which wraps every 16 frames.

No SOH is invented before the pack reports one: soh_available gates the
webserver and MQTT so both say unknown rather than showing the 99% default as
if it had been read.

Cells the LBC reports as 0xFFFF are stored as 0, kept out of the min/max
search and published as JSON null over MQTT. Ending the cell transfer on the
cell count rather than a PCI byte pattern fixes an out-of-bounds write on an
all-sentinel reply from a bench BMS.

Add Growatt LV (GBLI-series) battery support

Growatt's low-voltage BMS CAN protocol (GBLI6532 and siblings) wasn't
covered - existing Growatt support here is for the ARK HV pack, and the
GROWATT-LV-CAN inverter driver only emulates this protocol toward a real
Growatt inverter, it doesn't consume it from a real battery.

This is a straight port of the decode side of a project that's been
running this exact protocol translation live against a real GBLI6532 and
a Solis hybrid inverter (via the existing PYLON-LV-CAN output, no changes
needed there): github.com/schmellic/growatt2solis. The frame layout, byte
order, and the specific bits used for charge/discharge-enable and pack
count were all confirmed against real capture data rather than the spec
alone - see the header comment for details, including one case (0x319's
own enable bits) where the spec-plausible reading doesn't match what a
real pack actually does.

fix(renault-zoe-gen1): transmit missing vehicle broadcast frames to satisfy LBC CAN-V monitors

The Renault Zoe Gen1 LBC (BMS) expects periodic heartbeats on CAN-V from its primary vehicle powertrain broadcast frames. In their absence, the LBC flags communication loss (U1000 / D000) and asserts its caution bit.

This commit adds cyclic transmission of the 4 essential missing vehicle broadcast frames:
- 0x19F @ 100ms: PEB Inverter operational status & DC bus ready
- 0x426 @ 100ms: EVC HV power distribution & DC-DC auxiliary budget
- 0x436 @ 100ms: EVC Vehicle status & 16-bit sequence counter
- 0x69F @ 1000ms: BCM Gateway alive token (71 30 28 2F)

Verified on hardware: UDS 0x19 0x02 0x0F returns 59 02 4F (0 active DTCs).

Fix power reporting, real capacity, and manufacturer name

Found live against a real GBLI6532 + Solis S6-EH1P8K-L-PLUS:

- max_charge_power_W/max_discharge_power_W were never set. The generic
  safety layer zeroes the *current* fields right back to 0 whenever the
  *power* fields read 0, so every current value the driver computed was
  silently discarded every cycle - the Solis saw a battery permanently
  reporting 0A in both directions.
- total_capacity_Wh/remaining_capacity_Wh were stuck at the datalayer's
  generic 30kWh/0Wh defaults. Now decoded from Growatt's 0x314 frame
  (already received but previously discarded), converted to Wh using
  the real pack voltage.
- PYLON-LV-CAN's manufacturer name ("BatEmuLV") failed the Solis's
  strict validation on the PYLON_LV battery profile ("Battery Name
  Failure"). Changed to "PYLON   ", matching what a genuine Pylontech
  battery sends and what growatt2solis already proved works against
  this same real Solis - see that project's config.h/translate.h.
  This is a default-behavior change for every inverter using
  PYLON-LV-CAN, not just this new Growatt LV battery, so flagging it
  clearly for review rather than folding it in silently.

All three confirmed fixed live: real current now flows correctly in
both directions, Total/Remaining capacity show accurate real values,
and the Solis's "Battery Name Failure" cleared immediately.

Fix PYLON-LV-CAN 0x359 over-current sign bug

The over-current error/warning checks compared reported_current_dA
(the datalayer's signed "+ = charging" convention) against the wrong
sign of their own limit, so the charge-current check actually fired
on ordinary discharge and vice versa. Most visible the instant
max_charge_current_dA reaches 0 (e.g. a full battery) - any discharge
current at all then satisfies "current <= -max_charge_current", firing
a false "charge over current" error/warning on every cycle.

Found and confirmed live: a real GBLI6532 at 100% SOC, discharging
normally, tripped a spurious BMS alarm on a real Solis. Root-caused to
this sign inversion, fixed, and confirmed the alarm clears immediately
on the real inverter with the fix in place. This affects every battery
using PYLON-LV-CAN, not just the new Growatt LV driver - this project's
own CLAUDE.md had already flagged this exact bug as a known risk
before today's testing surfaced it live.

Fix idle-at-full-charge edge case in the over-current checks

The previous fix compared reported_current_dA directly against the
charge/discharge limits with no margin. That's fine while actively
charging or discharging, but breaks at the natural "battery full and
idle" state: max_charge_current_dA is legitimately 0 once full, and
idle current is exactly 0 too, so "current >= limit" evaluates the
boundary 0 >= 0 as true - firing the same false charge-overcurrent
error/warning this whole fix was meant to remove, just from a more
common trigger (idle at 100%) than the original bug (discharging at
100%).

Adds the same +10 (1.0A) margin the discharge-error check already
had, to both charge checks and the discharge-warning check, so a
genuinely-zero limit at zero current no longer counts as "exceeding"
it.

Confirmed live: reproduced on a real Solis (BMS alarm returned at
100% SOC while idle, even with the first fix applied), traced to this
exact boundary condition, and confirmed clean afterward.

Fix SOL-ARK-LV-CAN 0x359 over-current sign bug

The two over-current bits in the Sol-Ark 0x359 frame were compared against
the wrong sign of their own limit. datalayer.h documents the current sign as
positive while charging and negative while discharging, so in
SOL-ARK-LV-CAN.cpp update_values():

- line 57 raised discharge over-current (byte 0, bit 7) when
  reported_current_dA rose above +max_discharge_current_dA, which is a
  charging current.
- line 67 raised charge over-current (byte 1, bit 0) when
  reported_current_dA fell below -max_charge_current_dA, which is a
  discharging current.

A full pack reports max_charge_current_dA 0, so the second check reduced to
"reported_current_dA <= 0" and latched the charge over-current bit for the
whole time the pack sat idle or supplied the house. The Sol-Ark reads that
bit as the battery having entered self-protection.

SOL-ARK-LV-CAN.cpp was copied from PYLON-LV-CAN.cpp and still carries its
"See Pylon protocol for example integration" comment. Pylon had the same
inversion and it was fixed in #2920; this applies the same correction to the
Sol-Ark copy, keeping the +50 dA margin this file already used on the
discharge side and giving the charge side the same margin so a full idle
pack no longer sits on the 0 >= 0 boundary.

test/solark_lv_overcurrent_tests.cpp publishes one 0x359 frame per case and
asserts the two bits directly. Six of its seven cases fail before this
change.

The BYD driver allocated and displayed 13 temperature channels, but the

OTA: the rollback report runs once the log sinks are on

report_ota_rollback() ran before init_stored_settings(), and that call is what
switches web, USB, syslog and SD logging on from stored settings. So the
warning line - the one that names which firmware failed and what is running
instead - went to no sink a user can read. The OTA_ROLLBACK event does survive,
and its text sends them looking for exactly the line that was dropped. A
rolled-back update therefore left the reason nowhere (v12.5.0 field report).

Both halves of the original placement still hold and are why this is a move
rather than a split: it must follow init_events(), because it raises an event,
and it must precede everything that can itself fail, so the reason survives a
boot that also goes badly. Reading stored settings is the one step that has to
come first, and it is early and cheap.

Held by ORDER, not by presence: both calls were always there, in the wrong
sequence, so the case compares their positions in setup() and also pins that
the report still comes after init_events(). Read off the source like its two
neighbours, because Software.cpp's setup() is not in the host binary.

OtaConfirmPlacement.TheRollbackReportRunsOnceLoggingIsConfigured by name and
nothing else. Host suite 291, 290 pass and the one pre-existing
OtaConfirmPlacement skip. clang-format 23.1.0 clean, no line over 120 columns.

Leaf: use a 32 bit current accumulator

The 1 s current accumulator was int64_t with a uint32_t sample count. One second
of 10 ms 0x1DB frames at the signal's full scale reaches about 102,000, so 32 bits
has four orders of magnitude of headroom and the mean no longer needs the 64 bit
division helpers.

The count is made signed at the same time: int32_t sum + uint32_t count would
promote the rounding arithmetic in update_values() to unsigned and turn every
discharge window into a large positive current.

Leaf: expose the safety current window through a Battery virtual

The safety layer reached into the Leaf driver directly: safety.cpp included
NISSAN-LEAF-BATTERY.h, tested user_selected_battery_type and static_cast the
battery pointer, which was also unguarded against a null battery. Replace that
with a virtual on Battery whose default returns the pack's published current, so
the check is unchanged for every driver that does not override it, and the Leaf
driver overrides it to hand back the extremes of its averaging window.

The window is now tracked as a max/min pair instead of a single worst-magnitude
sample. A second holding both a charge and a discharge excursion used to report
only the larger of the two; now the charge check sees the max and the discharge
check sees the min. Both accumulators start at zero, so a single-direction window
reports zero for the other side, which is neutral for both comparisons.

Because the virtual is on the base class, packs 2 and 3 are now covered as well:
the check weighs the worst excursion of any configured pack against the limits,
which are already the system-wide minimum across all of them. Previously only
pack 1 was consulted, so a spike on the second pack of a double battery setup was
invisible to it.

Leaf: keep the limit check on pack 1 only

The loop weighed the worst excursion of any pack against
datalayer.battery.status.max_charge_power_W. That only holds while that field is
the system-wide minimum across the packs, which it is today because
update_calculated_values() caps it in place before the safety layer runs.

It is about to stop holding. Once the per-pack and aggregate views are split, the
cap moves after update_machineryprotection() and the field becomes pack 1's own
limit, at which point the loop is wrong in both directions: a pack legitimately
inside its own generous limit trips the event against pack 1's tighter one, and a
pack over its own tight limit hides behind pack 1's generous one. Neither shows up
as a merge conflict.

Pack 1 only keeps both sides of the comparison on the same pack under either
meaning, which is also exactly what this check did before any of this. Packs 2 and
3 need their own comparison against their own limits and their own failure
counters; that belongs with the split, not here.

Battery::safety_current_range_dA() keeps selecting the datalayer struct by
battery_index even though only pack 1 asks for now. The default has to be right for
whichever instance is asked or the virtual is a trap for the next caller.

Divide once at the end when converting current to power

active_power_W was current_dA * (voltage_dV / 100), which throws away everything
below a whole Volt before it multiplies: a 386.0 V pack is spent as 380 V, a 399.9 V
one as 390 V. Every pack under-reported its power by up to 2.5%, and the web cards,
MQTT, ESP-NOW and the safety layer all read that figure.

Not Leaf specific - update_calculated_values() runs for every battery type, and all
three packs had it. AKASOL and GROWATT already multiply before dividing and are left
alone.

The two lines this PR added to the limit check had the same pattern, and there it
under-reported in the unsafe direction, making a real overshoot harder to trip.

current_dA_to_power_W() goes in datalayer.h so the aggregate work can take it from
there rather than carrying its own copy.

Add a CI guard for the capacity detection list

battery_detects_capacity() is exact and cheap, but nothing stops a new
driver from assigning total_capacity_Wh and never being added to it. The
settings page would then keep offering a Battery capacity edit that the
driver overwrites moments later - the exact bug the switch exists to
prevent, reintroduced silently. No compiler or unit test can see it.

tools/check_capacity_detection.py derives the set from the sources
instead: it finds every `info.total_capacity_Wh =` in the drivers,
attributes it to the enclosing class, propagates through inheritance
(MqbEvoBattery reuses MebBattery's update_values), maps classes back to
BatteryType through create_battery(), and diffs that against the switch.
It reports drift in both directions and runs on every PR.

Deriving the set independently also confirms the list this series added:
the script agrees on all 35 integrations with nothing left over.

Even out the card padding and drop the red cross on Rescale SOC

A button is inline-block, so its bottom margin counts towards the height
of the line box it sits in. Inside a row that margin is dead space under
the button: it spaces the rows apart from below, and on the last row of a
card it lands between the button and the card's bottom padding. That is
why every card had a visibly bigger gap below its last row than above its
first one - most obvious on the single row "Fake battery voltage" card,
where the asymmetry is the whole card.

h4 button { margin-bottom: 0 } takes it out, so rows are spaced by the h4
margin alone and the gap above the first row and below the last are both
padding plus that one margin. The h4 margin comes down to 0.35em on top
of that, tightening the rows further. One number, 0.35em, now controls
row spacing everywhere on the page.

Rescale SOC drew its cross through .inactiveSoc, which is red - it reads
as a fault rather than as "off". The identical row below it, Manual
charge voltage limits, never had the class and has always drawn white, so
the span and its SOC_SCALING_CLASS handler are gone rather than recoloured.
Red stays where it is a warning: manual balancing and the charger rows.

Seed the fake battery from the hardware RNG

TestFakeBattery::setup() seeded from analogRead(0). GPIO0 is ADC2_CH1 on the
classic ESP32, but on the ESP32-S3 it is not an ADC pin at all, so every
instance logged "Pin 0 is not ADC pin!" at boot on all three S3 boards.

The failed read returns 0, so the fake cell spread was seeded identically on
every boot; esp_random() fixes that too.

Let library discovery respect the preprocessor guards

PlatformIO's library dependency finder defaults to chain mode, which scans
#include directives textually and does not evaluate conditionals. A header
included only under an #ifdef is therefore registered as a dependency of every
environment, whether or not that environment can reach it.

Two places in the tree do this today. sdcard.h includes <SD.h> under
#ifdef SDCARD, which only lilygo_330 and dfrobot_edge101_330 define, and
mdns.cpp includes <ESPmDNS.h> under #ifndef SMALL_FLASH_DEVICE. chain+ scopes
both to the environments that actually use them.

Whether that translates into smaller binaries depends on whether the linker was
pulling those objects out of the archive in the first place, so the firmware
size report on this PR is the measurement.
